newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Sept 16, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - International Business Machines Corp will roll out several security initiatives next month that will include a new way to build encryption into software that would let U.S. companies to export products with more security, PC Week reported in its Sept. 16 issue.
Intel Corp is designing PCI chip sets that will act as the high-octane fuel for its forthcoming P55C chip and Klamath processor engine, PC Week reported Sept. 16.

INFOWORLD - Novell Inc will unveil at the Network World/InterOp show this week support for Internet protocols in its core NetWare operating system and a plan for NetWare to run better with Microsoft Corp's Windows NT.

Microsoft Corp will unveil this week its Windows CE operating system that will run on hand-held computers, code-named Pegasus, and a vision that will extend far beyond personal digital assitants, InfoWorld reported Sept 16.

INFORMATION WEEK - Microsoft Corp's "Memphis" release of the Windows 95 operating system, including Internet Explorer version 4.0, could be available as early as mid-1997, Information Week reported in its Sept 16 issue.
After a three-year buying spree, Cisco Systems Inc has moved from routers into every part of the network hardware industry, Information Week said.

INTERACTIVE WEEK - CompuServe Corp last week gutted its marketing budget of more than $100 million, is raising questions about its resolve for staying independent in the online services business, InterActive Week reported in the Sept 17 issue.

The Clinton administration, stymied by efforts to pass new laws covering copyright online, appears to be on a collision course with Congress and the online industry over a United Nations treaty that oppononents fear could cripple further development of the Internet, Interactive Week reports.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Microsoft Corp will release the first beta version of its long-awaited Microsoft Transaction Server software code named Viper within the next two weeks, CRN reported in its Sept 17 issue.

Computer resellers angered by Microsoft Corp's bundling of its Office suite with Dell Computer Corp and Gateway 2000 PCs at 50 percent less than other resellers will get no satisfaction from the software giant, CRN reported.

COMPUTERWORLD - Rockwell International's Semiconductors Systems is preparing a 56 kilobit per second modem chip set that analysts said will enable faster access to the Internet and corporate data networks from remote sites and mobile workers' computers, Computerworld reported on Sept. 16.

Internet has experienced a number of noticeable slowdown over the past two weeks, and vexed users are pitching theories that range from overtaxed routers to a September surge of student use, Computerworld reported on Sept 16.

COMPUTER RETAIL WEEK - Mass disk storage prices are plummeting and consumers are flocking to computer retailers for applications to enable Internet access and desktop publishing, CRW reported in the Sept 16 issue.

The U.S. market may be on the cutting edge of computer technology but not when it comes to the stripped down world of network computers, as U.S. consumers wait while Japanese consumers can now buy a Pippin for $600, CRW reported.

MACWEEK - Adobe Systems Inc's Photoshop 4.0, the newest version of its popular graphics program, has only a modest amount of revisions, but the changes are worthwhile improvements, MacWeek reported in its Sept 16 issue.

The bulk of changes in Photoshop 4.0, which will ship for $895 in the fourth quarter, have gone into interface enhancements giving Photoshop easier accessibility like Adobe PageMaker and Adobe Illustrator, MacWeek reported.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - As the semiconductor industry heads toward the close of 1996, market forecasters are delivering some sobering news that the world market for computer chips may be shrinking, according to market researchers at Semico Research Corp, EBN reported Sept 16.

The U.S. and Japanese semiconductor industries are close to resolving some unfinished business on dumping provisions that was not addressed in last month's trade agreement, sources told Electronic Buyers' News in the Sept 16 issue.
